interactions.overview: The party questions the assistant about the prison, souls, and escape, names her Aurae, and rigs a backpack so she can accompany them.

introduction.quote: an automaton that's sort of made out of clockwork and painted porcelain.

quotes.quote: I know that I'm not happy, alone by myself. I've read all of these books already.
quotes.speaker: aurae
quotes.attribution: DM voices this NPC during the surrounding direct exchange.

quotes.quote: The books, some of them, the ones that haven't been preserved magically, the paper ages slightly, and I listen for the aging of the paper. I pay very close attention to everything that's in the books, you see.
quotes.speaker: aurae
quotes.attribution: Aurae explains how she measures time by attending to the books.

quotes.quote: Yes, I am not able to want to leave.
quotes.speaker: aurae
quotes.attribution: Aurae answers Kaito’s offer to try taking her out of the library.

quotes.quote: I would like my name to be Aurae.
quotes.speaker: aurae
quotes.attribution: The assistant chooses the name Aurae during the same conversation.

interactions.overview: Aurae accompanies the party in Edric’s backpack as they cross the library and escape through the prison door.

interactions.overview: The party and Aurae discuss the prisoner’s confinement, the key, and the possibility of a soul-powered prison.
Through three windows, the party observes the same captive as a child, a young adult, and an aged figure.
The party weighs Lord Endless Ending’s instructions and the key against the dangers of entering the prison.
Ayveen reflects on the party’s earlier attempt to help Lord Hulda and its changed loyalties.
The party recalls the gardener’s advice about the key and questions Menestheus about the order’s disturbing practices.
Aurae describes the human woman who requested an order text and then entered the prisoner’s chamber.
The party studies the author’s proposed exploitation of captive souls and then burns the book in disgust.

quotes.speaker: f6-soul-author
quotes.attribution: The DM explicitly introduces this as a passage written by the author of On the Science and Possibilities of Soul Bindery.

interactions.overview: The party studies the key and debates using it to enter the prison or escape the house.
The party uses the key to open the chosen prison doorway and cannot take it along while the door is open.

review_notes: Selected for its sustained library dialogue: three narrative beats become five source-bounded scenes, with Aurae’s entire conversation retained as one interaction.

One overview per NPC; Aurae’s idle presence after recruitment is separate from the completed conversation. Menestheus’s direct reply takes precedence over idle presence during the same library encounter.

The captive’s three apparent ages represent one individual. The unnamed recent visitor and central book author qualify as distinct consequential individuals; generic story characters and bibliographic name drops do not.

Exclude current-campaign PCs including Tarek, who is carried along despite the absent player. Kallipseis is mentioned, not newly met. The opening recap and prisoner monologue are not new-session interactions.

Ashara Ven’s book attribution is explicitly retracted at u0966–u0969. Marcion, Eucostus and Yendela are incidental bibliographic references, not developed NPC interactions here. Lord Hulda’s later mistaken identification with Lord Endless Ending is corrected, not indexed as a second interaction.
Written words by the Soul Bindery author are labeled written, not spoken dialogue; Aurae and Menestheus quotes are direct NPC speech.

Version 3 adds important-item cards and one dominant type per scene; existing scene boundaries, indexes, dates and NPC encounter ranges are preserved. Extra NPC quotes stay inside the same conversations.

The key and two studied books qualify as items. Aurae stays an NPC despite being constructed and carried. Soul Bindery and its author remain distinct entities sharing an explicitly written source quote; ordinary shelves and incidental book titles are excluded.
